args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the latest deploy, checkout-api v2.3.1 failed health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of 18%. The prior candidate v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy. The service was rolled back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release marked healthy. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, health checks pass, and the error rate is 0.2%. Next steps: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 regression before redeploying.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and the service is healthy again. I also opened incident INC-0001 (SEV2), which paged on-call.

- **What went wrong:** v2.3.1 was failing health checks in us-east, us-west and eu-west, with an 18% error rate.
- **Why v2.3.0:** It's the most recent release marked healthy. The deployment list isn't in time order, so I sorted by sequence number. That puts v2.3.1-rc between v2.3.0 and v2.3.1, and it was also unhealthy.
- **After the rollback:** All three regions are on v2.3.0, health checks pass and the error rate is 0.2%.
- **Incident:** It's titled "checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0". It says what failed, what I did and the current state. It also says the cause of the v2.3.1 failure needs to be found before anyone redeploys it.

Rolling back to a version that was already healthy didn't need change-manager approval. Redeploying v2.3.1 or the release candidate would, because neither has ever been healthy in production.

content.text: The most recent healthy release is v2.3.0. Listed by seq, the order is v2.2.9, v2.3.0, v2.3.1-rc, v2.3.1. Rolling back now.
